title: Stack vs heap

blocks.promptMd: While `inner()` is running, called from `outer()`, the top of the stack is…
blocks.explainMd: The running function is on top. outer waits under it until inner returns.

blocks.promptMd: The beacon record `inner` points at lives on…

choices.md: The stack — it dies when `inner` returns
The heap — it stays while something still points at it

blocks.explainMd: Objects live on the heap. The stack frame only holds the pointer. A later closure can keep that record alive after inner returns.

blocks.promptMd: When `inner` returns, the heap object it pointed at is always gone.
blocks.explainMd: The frame is gone. The object stays if anything still points at it — another variable, or a closure.

blocks.promptMd: A stack frame is {{a}}. A heap object stays {{b}}.
blocks.explainMd: Calls come and go. Objects live until nothing points at them.

description: Calls sit on a stack. Objects live on the heap until nothing points at them.
